title: Developmental Differences in Risk Patterns Among Children and Adolescents: A Latent Profile Analysis
abstract: Abstract Guided by the bioecological model of human development, this study used a person-centered method to examine the underlying risk patterns between children and adolescents. Using a nationally representative dataset ( n = 36,905), the Latent Profile Analysis explored risk across five domains (individual, family, school, neighborhood, and sociocultural) and compared them between children and adolescents. Children were exposed to low risk (83%), safety risk (6%), and school risk (10%) while adolescents were exposed to low risk (78%), individual risk (9%), and comprehensive risk (13%). As the developmental stages differ between children and adolescents, the risk across domains presented different patterns between the two age groups. Findings suggest that a more nuanced approach should be considered for children and adolescents considering their developmental stages.
